decisions.title: Product scope and first customers
decisions.exact: Initial segment, locations, currencies, enabled modules and capability promises
decisions.meaning: Choose who the first supported product is for and what you will promise them. A country choice alone does not select the customer type or authorize a live launch.
decisions.confirmed: Cameroon first, later CEMAC expansion, pre-production/demo data and phased implementation are confirmed. Customer sector, entity type, site count, currencies and first-release modules are not yet selected. [S3]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: select one defined Cameroon customer cohort and qualify online workflows first. Treat accounting and HR/payroll as separately gated capabilities. Use synthetic demonstrations until the relevant acceptance evidence is available.
decisions.alternatives: A narrow cohort limits test combinations and support cost. Multiple sectors/sites at launch increase configuration, training and regression coverage. Do not assume every implemented module is promised.
decisions.review: QA lead; domain owners for every promised capability
decisions.gate: R00 before the release-scope baseline; R33 still controls actual release.
decisions.evidence: Customer needs or pilot brief; entity and location inventory; capability matrix; current package acceptance and exclusions. [S1, S2, S8]
decisions.deferral: Individual capabilities may be excluded with a reason and owner. The target cohort and explicit release boundary cannot remain ambiguous when R00 is accepted.
questions: Which sector, business/entity type and intended customer cohort?
Which locations, number of sites and user roles?
Which transaction, functional and reporting currencies? Refer the policy to D02.
Which modules are required for the first cohort? List each.
Which accounting/payroll/tax outputs are promised, conditional or excluded?
What is demo only, controlled pilot, later release or out of scope?

decisions.title: Accounting policy choices
decisions.exact: Functional currency, rate/rounding, partial-year, close and year-end policies
decisions.meaning: Agree the accounting rules against which the implementation and reports will be assessed. A green test is not an accountant approving the underlying policy.
decisions.confirmed: Cameroon is the first jurisdiction. No functional-currency policy, rate source, rounding method, fiscal calendar or close policy has been approved in this pack. [S3, S4]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: have the accounting owner and qualified accountant document the policy for the selected entity and reporting framework, using explicit examples. Keep unsupported currency/reporting cases unavailable until mappings and source amounts are verified.
decisions.alternatives: Single-currency scope reduces conversion cases. Multi-currency scope requires approved rate authority, dates, missing-rate handling and reproducible conversion/rounding. Close-only locking and professionally qualified close have different evidence requirements.
decisions.review: Qualified accountant; engineering verifies the implementation against approved examples
decisions.gate: R02, R06, R07 and R20 before financial implementation acceptance.
decisions.evidence: Entity/framework applicability; rate-source evidence; calculation examples; fiscal-year setup; journal/report tie-outs; close, reopening and correction controls. [S1, S2, S4]
decisions.deferral: The detailed policy may remain pending during development, with a named reviewer and due gate. Affected financial outputs cannot be represented as qualified.
questions: What entity/sector and accounting/reporting framework applies?
Functional/reporting currencies; FX source, rate date and missing-rate rule?
Precision and rounding method at line, tax, journal and report levels?
Year start/end; first partial year and period boundaries?
What blocks close; who locks/reopens; how are corrections and reversals handled?
Required adjustments, opening balances and statements; attach reviewed examples.

decisions.title: Offline operating limits
decisions.exact: Offline devices, storage/eviction, supported tenders, fiscal limits and recovery
decisions.meaning: Decide whether offline selling is in scope and the exact devices, payments and recovery limits that must be proven before admitting it.
decisions.confirmed: The current continuation does not qualify a complete offline pilot. No supported device/tender matrix is approved here. [S2, S3]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: defer live offline admission until R04/R05 data-conservation evidence and R32 device/pilot criteria pass. Continue controlled engineering tests with synthetic data.
decisions.alternatives: Online-only admission has a narrower recovery surface. A controlled offline pilot adds device enrollment, storage loss, retries, uncertain payments, fiscal and support obligations. Browser storage alone is not a durability guarantee.
decisions.review: Security owner and country owner; QA and support for device/recovery evidence
decisions.gate: R04/R05 design; finalize before R32 offline admission.
decisions.evidence: Browser/OS/device matrix; capacity and eviction tests; replay/conservation tests; tender/provider/fiscal review; operator recovery drill. [S1, S2]
decisions.deferral: If offline is excluded, record that decision and prohibit offline capability promises/admission. Reopen D03 before enabling it; do not mark the capability verified.
questions: Defer offline, controlled pilot, or request qualified release?
Exact device models, OS and browser versions; enrollment/revocation owner?
Queue/capacity limits, eviction detection, older-client shutdown and export policy?
Which tenders are allowed offline; how are uncertain outcomes resolved?
Which local fiscal/numbering restrictions need country review?
Lost device, interrupted sync, duplicate/lost-response recovery and support steps?

decisions.title: Access privacy and retention
decisions.exact: Role matrix, legal holds, retention and HR/workforce disclosure
decisions.meaning: Specify who can see and change each class of data, what must be retained, and how sensitive workforce information is protected.
decisions.confirmed: Current work uses test/demo data. No production retention schedule, complete access matrix or employee disclosure policy is approved in this pack. [S3]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: use minimum role-based access, explicit employee/manager/accountant scopes and controlled export permissions. Keep payroll details restricted and define legal-hold precedence before adopting deletion schedules.
decisions.alternatives: Broad convenience access increases disclosure risk and review burden. More granular access requires role testing and support procedures. Retention periods must follow entity/data applicability review, not a guessed universal duration.
decisions.review: Application security; qualified legal/privacy advice for applicable retention and disclosure duties
decisions.gate: R08, R10, R16 and R28 before enforcement acceptance and sensitive launch.
decisions.evidence: Data inventory and classification; role/tenant/action matrix; employee disclosure rules; retention and hold sources; export and access-revocation tests. [S1, S2]
decisions.deferral: Missing policy blocks affected sensitive use or deletion. Record the exact restricted data/actions and reviewer due date; pre-production status alone does not prove every record is synthetic.
questions: For each role: view/change/approve/export rights and organization/employee scope?
Who may see salary, identity, health/leave documents and bank details?
What can employees, managers, HR and delegated accountants access?
Schedule by record class, authority source, start trigger and archive owner?
Who imposes/releases holds; how do holds override deletion and backups?
Permitted recipients, purpose, masking, audit trail and revocation process?

decisions.title: Country review and external authority
decisions.exact: Named country experts, rule versions, providers and submission authority
decisions.meaning: Name qualified people to review each regulated capability and identify who can authorize real provider operations or statutory submissions.
decisions.confirmed: Cameroon-first source research exists, with unresolved current-law interpretation and reviewer requirements. Source discovery is not statutory approval. No expert appointments or provider/submission authority are confirmed here. [S4]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: review accounting, tax, payroll/labour, social insurance and fiscal/declaration capabilities separately. Bind each approval to a rule version, applicable entity/employee cases and independent expected examples.
decisions.alternatives: Prepare exports for authorized human review, or later qualify direct submission through a named provider/authority. These are distinct capabilities; approving one does not authorize the other.
decisions.review: Qualified Cameroon accounting, tax, payroll/labour and social-insurance expertise as applicable; independent technical reviewer
decisions.gate: Begin appointments at R00; complete per capability at R18/R19 before activation.
decisions.evidence: Qualifications and appointments; current source snapshots; rule/version/effective-date map; reviewed fixtures; provider acceptance and submission mandates. [S1, S4, S5, S6]
decisions.deferral: Record missing experts/sources/providers as unresolved. Keep that regulated capability or real submission unavailable; independent engineering may continue.
questions: Which accounting, payroll, tax, CNPS, fiscal or declaration capabilities?
For each capability: real reviewer, qualification, Cameroon scope and independence?
Exact pack/rule version, sources, effective dates and customer applicability?
Who independently checks normal, boundary and exception examples?
Provider/account/capability and sandbox/live environment; credential reference only?
Who may prepare, approve and execute each real payment or filing?

decisions.title: Optional feature priorities
decisions.exact: Which optional lot/landed-cost/assets/budget/cohort features are required
decisions.meaning: Choose which optional extensions are justified by an actual customer need. A promised optional feature becomes required for that cohort.
decisions.confirmed: No acceptance of R34–R37 optional capabilities is established by the general modernization request. [S1, S8]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: assess each feature independently and defer those without a named customer decision, usable source data and measurable acceptance scenario.
decisions.alternatives: A bounded extension can satisfy a real sector requirement but adds implementation and assurance work. Deferral protects delivery focus; it also forbids promising that feature for the selected cohort.
decisions.gate: R34–R37 before committing implementation capacity; earlier if promised to the first cohort.
decisions.evidence: Customer requirement, source-data assessment, bounded feature definition, cost/effort review and acceptance example. [S1, S8]
decisions.deferral: Required / deferred / not applicable must be recorded for each feature, with reason and reassessment trigger. Do not treat all optional features as one yes/no decision.
questions: Lot/serial/expiry and unit conversion: required, deferred or not applicable; why?
Landed cost and replenishment: scope, customer need and source quality?
Asset subledger/automation: material customer requirement and accounting owner?
Budgets and scenario cash forecasting: decisions supported and data required?
Cohort/retention analytics: business purpose and identity/consent constraints?
For each accepted feature: cohort, owner, acceptance example, effort and due gate?

decisions.title: Operational service objectives
decisions.exact: Deployment workload, latency, error, backlog, cost, RPO/RTO and alert objectives
decisions.meaning: Agree the operating conditions and measurable service limits before judging operational readiness. RPO means acceptable data-loss window; RTO means acceptable recovery time.
decisions.confirmed: Current evidence does not qualify a fresh integrated build/package, complete browser journeys or production recovery. No measured production service objectives are approved here. [S2, S3]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: first measure representative workloads in a controlled environment, then agree explicit thresholds and measurement windows with product, finance and SRE. Do not publish unmeasured service promises.
decisions.alternatives: Tighter latency/recovery targets generally require more capacity, recovery automation and support expenditure. A smaller bounded cohort may reduce the initial operating envelope but still needs measured acceptance.
decisions.review: Product owner and finance owner; independent QA/technical evidence review
decisions.gate: R23/R30 before measuring operational acceptance against agreed limits.
decisions.evidence: Deployment topology; workload model; reproducible baseline measurements; restore drill; worker/backlog monitoring; alert delivery and cost model. [S1, S2]
decisions.deferral: Leave unknown thresholds blank with a measurement owner/date. That service promise remains unqualified. Record zero silent event loss, duplicate economic effects and unauthorized access as proposed invariants, not measured achievements.
questions: Hosting/topology; tenant/user concurrency, data volume and peak transactions?
Critical journeys, percentile/window, acceptable latency and error-rate thresholds?
Queue age/backlog/throughput targets and escalation conditions?
RPO and RTO per service/data class; how will restore be measured?
Budget, measurement unit/window, alert recipient and escalation response?
Test dataset, duration, observer, evidence location and remeasurement trigger?

decisions.title: Pilot admission and observation
decisions.exact: Pilot cohorts, minimum volume, business-cycle coverage and observation window
decisions.meaning: Define a fair pilot test in advance: participants, duration, business cycles, acceptance evidence and stop conditions.
decisions.confirmed: Cameroon is prioritized. No named pilot customer, transaction-volume threshold, observation window or pilot authorization has been confirmed. [S3]
decisions.recommendation: Proposed: admit a bounded cohort only after its applicable security, data, country and provider gates pass. Agree the pilot criteria before seeing the results; keep online and offline admission distinct.
decisions.alternatives: A shorter/narrower pilot costs less but cannot demonstrate unobserved business cycles. Broader admission needs more support and evidence. A synthetic rehearsal is useful but does not establish real-customer pilot performance.
decisions.review: Product, QA and relevant domain owners; country/provider reviewers for regulated or external capabilities
decisions.gate: Before R32/R33; criteria must not be invented after results.
decisions.evidence: Named cohort and permitted capabilities; signed criteria; support/rollback plan; representative business-cycle evidence; gate matrix and independent review. [S1, S2]
decisions.deferral: Pilot may be deferred while engineering continues. No admission or release approval follows from a draft plan or successful rehearsal.
questions: Which R packages and country/provider approvals must pass first?
Which sales, returns, close, payroll and reporting cycles must be observed?
Minimum volume per workflow, duration/window and who sets the threshold?
Stop criteria, incident owner, data reconciliation and rollback/support plan?
Who reviews results, accepts residual limits and separately authorizes release?
